notes:
The relevant statistics are available at different administrative units:
Planning region There are 5 regions in Singapore. Median size: 136.41 km²
Planning area There are 55 planning areas in Singapore. Planning areas have about 50,000 to 250,000 residents. Median size: 10.60 km²
Subzone There are 332 subzones in Singapore. The average subzone has around 10,000 to 30,000 residents, but the largest has >100,000. Median size: 1.19 km²
The map's population data is grounded on 3 main datasets, all from the 2025 General Household Survey: - **Employed** residents by **planning area** of **residence** _(base employed residence statistic)_. - Resident population by **subzone** of **residence** _(to refine employed residences)_. - **Employed** workers by **planning area of workplace**, broken out by **planning region of residence** _(for workplaces and O/D)_. Links to the tables are in the same order in the Data Source Links section below. --- Population statistics are first extrapolated to final working-population totals (including foreign workforce and excluding invalid resident employment). Employed residence counts are pushed down to the **subzone** level by splitting a planning area's employed residents proportionally to subzones based the subzone's number of residents. Buildings are obtained from Overture Maps and then filtered for demand-relevant buildings. Building types are coarsely classified based on OSM building types (via Overture) and [Singapore's Masterplan zoning](https://eservice.ura.gov.sg/maps/?service=MP), to: residential low/med/high, commercial, office, industrial low/med/high. Floorspace is estimated using a mix of building footprint + height, as well as the plot's max allowed floorspace serving as an upper bound. Residence and workplace statistics are then distributed down to these buildings, weighted by estimated floorspace and a set of manual coefficients. Special workforce demand is first injected before per-building distribution, with their workforce counts subtracted from subzonal totals to prevent double counting. Per-building demand points are then aggregated with a minimum 200 m spacing. Aggregated demand points with less than 50 people are merged into nearby points. Commute flows are assigned using a gravity model constrained by the O/D matrix for (workplace planning area ⟷ residence planning region). Special non-workforce demand is then finally added onto the existing demand data. Non-university/airport points are merged with existing points if necessary. More comprehensive descriptions are available on the [repo's README](https://github.com/Zeepheru/subwaybuilder-singapore-map).
